sentences.text: Mr. Naresh vs State Of Telangana on 11 November, 2024

The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice K. Sujana
 Criminal Petition No.6832 Of 2024
Order:

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') to quash the proceedings against the petitioner/accused No.5 in C.C.No.1405 of 2021 on the file of I-Additional Junior Civil Judge-cum-V-Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Ranga Reddy at L.B.Nagar.

entities.text: I-Additional Junior Civil Judge-cum-V-Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Ranga Reddy
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Sections 406, 420, 468, 471, 506 and 120-B of Indian Penal Code (for short 'I.P.C').
2.

The facts of the case are that the de facto complainants/respondents 2 and 3 filed a complaint on 21.06.2019, wherein it is stated that the complainants are the absolute owners and possessors of land admeasuring 2561 Sq yards in Plot No.61 of Nacharam village, IDA, Kapra Municipality, Ranga Reddy District.
It is in the name of their partnership firm M/s.Amar Roto Prints.

In the year 2015,
respondents 2 and 3 thought of disposing of the said property and partnership firm and looking for prospective purchasers, their watchman who is looking over the said property informed them that some persons came to the said property and on enquiry, he came to know that the said persons are the bank officials of South India Bank, Ameerpet Branch.
When the complainants went to the said Bank and enquired with the Branch Manager, they came to know that A.1 and A.2 took loan of Rs.32 Crores and also taken CCOL adhoc of Rs.3,50,00,000/.

As they failed to pay the said amount to the Bank and committed default, in violation of the terms and conditions agreed by them, the security interest created in respect of immovable property in favour of bank have become Non- Performing Assets and after verifying the copies of documents furnished to them, they came to know that Sanjay Gupta, Kiran Gupta and Naresh the then Branch Manager of South India Bank and A.3, A.4 and A.5 colluded with each other and in pursuance of their criminal conspiracy, they have created fake and forged the document of Reconstitution of Firm dated 30.03.2016 and obtained loan.
As such they were cheated by A.1 to A.5 and requested to take action against them.

After investigation, the police filed charge sheet against A.1 to A.5.
3.

Heard Sri Vikram Poosarla, learned Senior Counsel appearing for G.P.Yashvardhan, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri D.Arun Kumar, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent No.1 and Sri Naresh Sunkara, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.3.

4. The contention of learned counsel for the petitioner is that the brother of respondents 2 and 3 being the continuing partner in particular the Managing partner of the firm was well aware of the purportedly fabricated reconstitution deed dated 30.03.2016 and had approached the Bank along with A.1 and A.2 on numerous occasions and he was aware of the loan sanctioned and was present during creation of mortgage.
With effect from 01.05.2017 the loan account of borrower Company was classified as NPA as they have failed to pay the debt.

Accordingly, the Bank officials issued demand notice on 10.07.2017 and symbolic possession was taken on 25.09.2017 during which time,

sentences.text: Thus, respondents 2 and 3 were aware of the purported fabrication and mortgage in the year 2017, however failed to take any action till June, 2019.
Further, the Bank took physical possession of all the properties, and auctioned certain properties mortgaged by the Borrower Company and recovered an amount of Rs.20,05,00,000/-.
The Bank also filed O.A.No.871 of 2019 before the Debt Recovery Tribunal claiming Rs.28,07,33,838.96/- and the outstanding as on date is Rs.32.20 Crores.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioners further contended that S.A.No.36 of 2021 before the Debts Recovery Tribunal-II, Hyderabad was filed and I.A.No.254 of 2021 was also filed seeking stay of all proceedings pursuant to the order dated 06.01.2021 passed by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Cyberabad, Ranga Reddy at L.B.Nagar in Crl.M.P.No.4 of 2021, was dismissed by the Tribunal.

entities.text:
Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Cyberabad, Ranga Reddy
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The main allegation against the petitioner is that he in collusion with other accused created and fabricated the reconstitution partnership deed dated 30.03.2016.
However, on the date of execution of the said reconstitution deed, petitioner was not posted in Ameerpet Branch of the Bank and he joined in the said Branch on 18.04.2016.
He further contended that respondents 2 and 3 admitted that they have knowledge of alleged fabrication in September, 2017 but failed to take action till 2019.
Therefore, the proceedings against the petitioner are not at all maintainable as respondent Nos.2 and 3 have not approached the Court with clean hands.
Petitioner is an employee of Bank has nothing to do with the present crime, more so, he has joined only on 18.04.2016 much after the alleged forged document.
Therefore, Sections 406, 420, 468, 471, 506 and 120-B of I.P.C, are not attracted to the petitioner.
As such, prayed the Court to quash the proceedings against the petitioner.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.3 would submit that there are serious allegations against the petitioner which requires trial.
It is not the stage to decide whether petitioner joined the Bank after the alleged forgery, has to be decided by the trial Court after full-fledged trial.

As such, prayed the Court to dismiss this petition.
7.
In view of the submissions made by both the Counsel and the material on record, the allegations against the petitioner are that he is the Bank Manager at the time of alleged offence.
He colluded with A.1 and A.2 to cause loss to respondents 2 and 3.

Further, the charge sheet filed by the police shows specific allegations against this petitioner that he wantonly did not submit the deed of reconstitution of firm to the legal advisor, as it is forged.

The petitioner has taken supplementary opinion from the same legal advisor on 16.05.2016 and even in that the legal advisor noticed that the deed of reconstitution deed dated 30.03.2016 is an un-registered document and petitioner was advised to get it registered under the Registration Act.

Inspite of that, petitioner sanctioned loan in favour of A.1 and A.2, without proper verification from Registration of Firms to check with the original partners before processing the loan to sanction the same, which shows that there are specific allegations against this petitioner that even though he was not in the Branch on 30.03.2016,
thereafter the legal advisor informed him that the said document is not a registered document and it has to be compulsorily registered and that it is a forged document.
Being a Bank Manager he kept the forged fabricated document for loan processing without verifying with the actual land owners of the said partnership firm.

The investigation reveals that the petitioner is also having knowledge Mr. Naresh vs State Of Telangana on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5911254/
2 about the alleged forgery, inspite of that being a responsible person has not taken any steps.

entities.text: Mr. Naresh vs State Of Telangana on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: All these issues are factual issues which require trial.
The trial Court has to decide the same after full-fledged trial.
Therefore, at this stage, it cannot be said that petitioner has no role in this crime.
There are no merits in this petition and the criminal petition is liable to be dismissed.
8. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is dismissed.
Miscellaneous petitions, pending, if any, shall stand closed.

K. SUJANA, J Date :11.11.2024 Rds Mr. Naresh vs State Of Telangana on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5911254/
